perennials/fa1508c:
The side view and the model stop being two unrelated pictures: both now
read the same shaped ground. Each figure gains a footing — the ground
under it, computed once in the page by the one interpolator — and the
elevation stands every plant at its own footing, so a tree in a dip
starts low and a bed on a bank starts high. The earth band becomes the
land's side-on skyline; the horizon line stays put as the datum the
rule measures from, dashed so it reads as a rule line wherever the
land leaves it. The scale fits the tallest reach and the deepest dip
together, and the rule grows below-zero ticks for a dug pond.

The exported sheet re-renders the same section from the same geometry
(sectionOf, earthPathD), draws her benchmarks on the plan, and prints
the ground's coverage line in the footer, so the client is handed the
ground she saw. A shaped ground now earns the band by itself: the
land's section is the claim the plan cannot draw. A yard with no
heights and no shaped ground renders exactly as before.
noodles/face545:
Two surfaces landed together because they share the arithmetic. The
ladder moved into the model (ladderPcs/ladderRungOf): the wheel's bloom
pads delegate to it, and the chord editor grew a rung row - triad 7 9 11
13 sus4 sus2 - that rebuilds the selected bar's stack with the exact
stacks the wheel writes, diatonic on degree roots and common-practice on
visitors. Collapsing to a plain diatonic triad hands the slot its degree
number back, so it keeps following the key.

The staff painter is now a grand staff: treble and bass joined by a
system line, each note routed to whichever staff needs fewer ledger
lines, both signatures (bass two steps lower), and the slash-bass cellar
becomes two civilized ledger lines instead of eight. The clefs are real
engraved outlines via Path2D (Wikimedia GClef.svg public domain,
FClef.svg CC BY 2.5), every open notehead carries its letter inside, the
chord slots adopt the engraving's bar columns so towers stand over the
slots they sound from, and the voice-leading threads draw between the
noteheads themselves - gold for held tones, dim slopes for moving
voices, wrap stubs at the loop seam. The separate vthreads strip is
deleted. The export plate rides the same painter.

Smoke: rung chips write a five-tone 9 and collapse back to the degree;
the strum assert now reports key and state when it fails. Oracle: ladder
stacks, alteration naming, sus collapse, rung detection.
noodles/fa4df3f:
Three roots, one symptom. A launch while playing marked the tapped scene
playing immediately even though it had only queued, and the next step
event snapped it back — the flash. The engine's immediate queue event
never reached the UI at all: scheduleVisual's stale-drop treated time 0
as an ancient event once the clock passed one second, so the queued paint
waited for the next step event to repeat it; time 0 is now exempt (it
means next-frame UI feedback), which also revives the stop event that
clears queues. And with the immediate paint alive, step snapshots still
in flight behind the 0.25 s visual lookahead landed after it and
flickered it off, so queue snapshots now carry an epoch the UI compares
before applying. The pulse itself moves off a free-running 0.9 s CSS
animation that dimmed the whole clip, repainted every frame, and
restarted mid-phase on any re-render: queued is a steady amber ring and
triangle, and the step events toggle the blink at the quarter note,
pinned to the heard beat like every other playback visual.
